description: In nearly planar scenes, sweep over angle or x-intervals to build a shortlist of bodies whose trajectories can come close during the next step. It turns broad-phase collision geometry into a gravitational encounter scheduler, so expensive local refinement is only spent on pairs that geometry says can matter.
mathematical_formalization: For each body i, build swept interval I_i = [phi_i^min - rho, phi_i^max + rho] or [x_i^min - rho, x_i^max + rho]; during a sweep-line pass, enqueue pair (i, j) whenever I_i intersects I_j and d_perp(i, j) < rho
analogical_connections: A sweep-line segment-intersection algorithm becomes an orbital close-pass shortlist.
Broad-phase collision detection becomes broad-phase gravitational encounter detection.
A rotating radar scan suggests selecting only objects that enter a tracking wedge.
implementation_hypothesis: Estimate one-step swept intervals after a tentative drift; sort interval endpoints; maintain an active set; emit candidate pairs only; pass the shortlist to encounter-aware integration rather than to a collision response system.
experiment_seed: Use a 2D asteroid belt and a narrow ring scene; compare candidate-pair recall and runtime against brute-force O(N^2) close-pass scans.

closest_prior_art.title: Algorithms for Reporting and Counting Geometric Intersections
REBOUND: An open-source multi-purpose N-body code for collisional dynamics
Symplectic integrators in the shearing sheet

novelty_claim: The key novelty is to use geometry not for collision response, but for deciding when gravitational integration should temporarily become more expensive.
differentiation: REBOUND's sweep is about collisions in elongated or ring-like systems. This concept redirects the same geometric idea into encounter triage and local solver escalation, so it is not just a collision detector copied into a new codebase.
experimental_result: Validated as a sparse deterministic trigger: recall stays at 1.0 on the sampled star-grazing rollout while the queue remains mostly inactive on the calm small-N ring case.
